settings.heading: Shop by how they sleep
settings.text: Every bed is filed under one of five sleep needs. Pick the one that sounds most like your dog.
settings.quiz_text: Answer four questions and we'll suggest a bed and a size.

settings.title: They circle and circle before lying down
settings.text: Circling is how dogs build a nest. Endless circling usually means the bed isn't giving them the shape, or the sides, they're looking for.

settings.title: They're slower to get up in the morning
settings.text: Morning stiffness gets more common with age. On a thin, flat bed, hips and elbows press through to the hard floor. A deep foam bed stops that.

settings.title: You can feel the floor through the middle
settings.text: Press your hand into the spot where they lie. If it sinks straight through, the filling has flattened and it's no longer doing its job.

settings.title: They pick the sofa, the rug, anywhere but their bed
settings.text: If they stretch out everywhere except their bed, it's usually too small, too enclosed or too soft to lie flat on.

settings.title: They squeeze into boxes, baskets and laundry piles
settings.text: Some dogs sleep best with something wrapped around them. On a flat, open bed they go looking for a box, a basket or the laundry pile instead.

settings.heading: Five signs it's time for a new bed
settings.text: Dogs don't complain about a bad bed. They stop using it, or they keep using it and feel it in the morning.

settings.question: How do I choose the right size?
settings.answer: Measure your dog from nose to base of tail while they're stretched out asleep, then add 15–20cm. That's the length of bed to look for. Curlers can go a little smaller and sprawlers should go bigger. The Sleep Match suggests a size in about a minute, and our size guide goes breed by breed.

settings.question: Which bed is best for an older dog?
settings.answer: Start with our Support beds: memory or orthopaedic foam that spreads their weight evenly, ideally with a low front they can step straight into. A bed isn't a treatment, so if your dog is stiff or sore, keep talking to your vet. A supportive surface does make the hours they spend lying down more comfortable.

settings.question: My dog gets anxious. Can a bed help?
settings.answer: Many nervous dogs settle more easily in a Calm bed. Raised, bolstered sides give them something to lean into and a wall at their back, a bit like curling up against a littermate. It won't cure anxiety, but it gives them a spot that's always theirs.

settings.question: Can I return a bed?
settings.answer: Yes. You have [returns_days] days from delivery to let us know, then 14 days to send it back unused and in its original packaging. We refund you as soon as it's back with us. Everything's on our Delivery & Returns page.

settings.question: Are the covers washable?
settings.answer: Many of our beds have removable, machine-washable covers. Each product page says how to care for that bed. For foam beds, wash the cover, never the foam.

settings.question: Do you deliver outside the UK?
settings.answer: Yes, to the EU and a number of other countries. International rates are shown at checkout before you pay.
